key: Notes: Roe at court 1615, Pelsaert came 1620, Mundy 1630-34, Thevenot reached Surat 1666 -> A, B, C, D (option A), not B.

x: All four are correct: Aurangzeb reimposed jizya in 1679, banned Navroz, banned music at court and had the Fatawa-i-Alamgiri compiled. Even so, Persian works on Indian music were written in his reign and he himself played the veena.
Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom (executed under Aurangzeb) was recalled in public commemorations in Dec 2025 and Apr 2026.
Golconda fell to Aurangzeb in 1687 and its last ruler Abul Hasan Qutb Shah (Tana Shah) was imprisoned, which ended Qutb Shahi rule over Andhra; Golconda became the 21st Mughal suba.

The Mansabdar got a rank and was paid by a tankhwah jagir; the jagirdar's agents collected the assessed revenue (jama) through the zamindars, who kept a hereditary share, and the peasant paid about one-third of the produce.
Tobacco and maize (and also chillies) came from the New World via the Portuguese. Pepper, spices, oilseeds, cotton, indigo, opium, rice, wheat and sugarcane were established Indian crops.
Makhfi is best known as the pen name of Zeb-un-Nissa, Aurangzeb's daughter; some notes give it for Nur Jahan, so 'Nur Jahan alone' is the trap.

The standard answer is Humayun's widow Haji Begum (Bega Begum), who commissioned the tomb in Akbar's reign (c.1565-72). Some notes name Hamida Banu Begum, Akbar's mother, but not as the sole builder; Gulbadan Begum wrote the Humayun-nama and Jahanara built the Jama Masjid at Agra.
Panch Mahal, the Jama Masjid and Jodha Bai's palace are at Fatehpur Sikri. The Moti Masjids are in Agra Fort (Shah Jahan) and the Red Fort, Delhi (Aurangzeb), not at Fatehpur Sikri.

Humayun's tomb introduced the double dome and shows calligraphy, arabesque and jali work. The Sheesh Mahal is known for mirror work (the charbagh is the four-quartered garden), Ram Bagh is Babur's first garden while pietra dura peaked at the Taj Mahal, and the double dome first appeared at Humayun's tomb, not the Taj.
